messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nguyen <chris.nguyen@lakeshorehealth.com>, Katie Morales <katie.morales@lakeshorehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Inference interop qualification + SDK change requests (post-demo)

Hi Chris / Katie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and what engineering will need to trial a small pilot: 

Summary of pain we heard
- Live triage use case has very bursty traffic; average request length ~450 tokens but 95th percentile runs up to 4k tokens when users paste long medical notes.
- Deterministic ranking and provenance matter: you need stable embeddings + rerank with audit traces for QA.
- Latency SLOs for the triage UI: target 400ms median, sub-second 95th for summary + rerank when on Dedicated capacity.

Goals we agreed on
1) Functional parity for current summarization + reranking flow (embedding -> approximate nearest neighbor -> rerank with model L1)
2) Prototype streaming summaries with function-calling hooks for structured triage output (diagnosis_codes, urgency_level, follow_up_required)
3) Validation criteria: accuracy on your 200-case prompt set + end-to-end 95th latency under 1s in pilot runs

Technical constraints / asks for Redwood to prepare
- SDK changes: lightweight streaming API that exposes both chunked text and structured function call events (we propose adding a streaming "funcall.event" envelope). See attached redwood-sdk-change-log.md for a minimal patch we think is required.
- Model variants: plan to test a quantized 8-bit variant for cost but keep a float32 fallback for high-cost/rare long sequences.
- Cache/Batching profile: explicit guidance on prefix caching TTLs (you mentioned many repeat templates) and an option to pin a "cold KV warmup" flag when seeding long-note requests.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-change-log.md (diff + example), sow-draft-v1.pdf (pilot SOW placeholder)

Proposed near-term plan
- Week 1: Redwood provides a branch of the SDK + example app that demos streaming funcall events and a rerank pipeline (we’ll include a simple ANN pipeline and re-ranking call).
- Week 2: Lakeshore runs 200-case evaluation locally (we provide a script to run against Dedicated sandbox) and reports accuracy/latency.
- End of Week 3: Sync to review results and calibrate acceptance criteria / pricing.

Please reply with any missing items. If that looks right I’ll loop in our infra engineer (Marissa) and Ben will prepare the pilot commercial terms.

Thanks,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nsharma@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Chris Nguyen <chris.nguyen@lakeshorehealth.com>

Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inference interop qualification + SDK change requests (post-demo)

Thanks Nikhil — solid recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Bursty traffic: the peak behavior is driven by nightly clinician uploads (batch import) and also by on-call hours (manual paste). For the pilot we can sample mixed traffic but want to see the Dedicated baseline for the worst-case bursts.
- 95th latency target: 1s overall is acceptable for pilot; for the UI we still want a progressive streaming summary so users see the first paragraph within ~250-400ms in normal cases.
- Embeddings stability: critical. Please confirm how Redwood handles embedding deduping across model variants (we need the same embedding vectors when we switch quantization / rollout).

On the SDK: the streaming funcall envelope looks promising. A couple requests:
1) include a simple schema example for the structured output we showed today (JSON schema for diagnosis_codes and urgency_level).
2) a small Node example (we are primarily Node/Express) for the streaming client with automatic reconnect/fallback to non-streaming.

We’ll run the 200-case eval and send over the test set by EOD tomorrow (we’ll scrub PII first). Last ask: can your team include a short runbook snippet we can show to our security team that describes data retention on Dedicated vs Hosted for the pilot?

-signed,
Chris

- Add JSON schema example for structured outputs (Marissa, include in drive folder)
- Provide short security runbook snippet about data retention and KMS flow for Dedicated sandbox (Marissa)
- Create pilot SOW draft with 4-week timeline and pricing bands (Ben)

Commercial notes / pricing options to propose
- Light pilot (4 weeks): Dedicated sandbox, 2 reserved GPU slots, $8k/month baseline; option to scale with burst on-demand.
- Production conversion: typical reserved capacity commitment (quarterly) with volume discounts for >10M tokens/month.

Risks & mitigations
- Long-sequence token cost: recommend testing quantized model first but reserve float fallback for very long notes (cost/latency trade-off).
- Embedding drift during quantized rollouts: we should perform embedding regression tests during rollouts and pin a "stable-embedding" model alias for production.
